diagnostic_differences: wolf muzzle projects farther and tapers toward a thicker terminal nose
wolf ears usually end in pointed tips
feline muzzle is shorter, deeper, and more parallel-sided with compact shadow
common_confusions: stylized large feline with tall ears
near_species_differences.correction_guidance: preserve canine forward muzzle projection, wedge shadow, pointed ear tips, and terminal nose depth while retaining approved markings and body plan

coverage_requirements.notes: prove eye, ear, muzzle, and nose architecture
prove counts, attachments, posture, and tail base

explicitly_absent_or_inapplicable.reason: baseline anthropomorphic gray wolf body plan has no wings
baseline anthropomorphic gray wolf body plan has no tentacles
baseline anthropomorphic gray wolf body plan has no horns or antlers

life_stages: juveniles have shorter limbs, smaller muzzle mass, and larger head-to-body ratio; this pilot subject is adult
sex_or_role_dimorphism: the pilot lineage permits proportion variation but does not change feature count or attachment topology
polymorphisms: coat value, eye color, ear height, tail length, and body build may vary within declared bounds
population_or_regional_variation: fur density and seasonal coat fullness may vary with climate
heritable_anomalies: ear notches, unusual markings, or digit variation require explicit individual declaration

feature_relationships.rule: eyes, ears, muzzle, and nose retain their named skull landmarks and scale together with head width and depth
each visible hand retains five declared digits and each visible claw remains attached to one terminal digit
the single tail emerges from the posterior pelvic centerline and follows pelvis motion without migrating

limits: tail supports balance but is not a grasping limb
read meanings from coordinated channels and scene context

invalid_generalizations: Do not add feline whisker pads, rounded feline ears, retractable claws, or a short deep feline muzzle.
Do not add extra tails, wings, horns, tentacles, eyes, ears, arms, legs, or digits.
Do not convert the digitigrade lower limbs into plantigrade human legs or ordinary quadruped legs.
Do not treat temporary injury, wetness, grooming, clothing, or emotional posture as species anatomy.
